title: StratoSort on an M4 Pro Mac with 24 GB: A Dry Run Before Any File Moved, Mixed Matching, and a Link to Another Local AI App over MCP

seo.title: StratoSort Hands-on Test: Mac File Sorting and MCP
seo.description: Hands-on test of StratoSort on a 24 GB M4 Pro Mac: dry run, per-file review, a 286-file move, mixed matching and a link to Loci over MCP.

faq: Does StratoSort move files before you approve them?
Not in the session. The five-file dry run said "Nothing has moved", and each file got a review card before the move. Whether every file was reviewed before the 286-file move is not recorded.
observed
How well did StratoSort sort the test files?

Mixed. In the dry run two of five files were assigned to a folder; in the review step a banner counted 126 uncategorized files; two Search Console exports went to the fallback although their folder was named as closest. No accuracy count was made.
measured
Can another AI app query StratoSort over MCP?

Yes, in the session. The Loci app connected, listed four tools and returned results from list_smart_folders and search_documents. The tester had to work out the connection himself; get_document_summary and chat_with_documents were not called.
observed
Does StratoSort rename files?
Yes, in the move list: original names were replaced by lowercase names with a date. The result was not checked on disk, and the rewording function was not tried.
observed
Is StratoSort private and offline?
The welcome screen says private and on-device, and the founder statement says no account and no telemetry. No network traffic was inspected and no offline run was tried, so this is not verified.
vendor-claim
What was not tested?

Undo, copy mode, Dashboard mode, AI and model settings, timing, memory, offline use and uninstall. The built-in document chat was opened only afterwards and its answers were not checked. The app version and the models used were not recorded.
observed
Does StratoSort have its own search and document chat (RAG)?

Yes. The developer says StratoSort indexes extracted file content locally, retrieves relevant material for a question and gives it to the model, so no other app or MCP is needed. On the Mac, press Cmd+K or click Knowledge OS to open Search, Chat, Relate, Atlas and Timeline. The tester opened Search, Chat, Timeline and Relate afterwards and saw a chat answer with source markers; he did not check whether the answer was correct. An earlier version of this page wrongly said a retrieval layer was missing.

verdict.general: An on-device file organizer by its own description, with safeguards the tester could see: a dry run, a per-file review before anything moves, and an MCP link that the app says only reads. In this session analysis, review and a file move were run (the end of the move is not recorded) and the MCP link worked from another local AI app, but matching was mixed and needs tuning. Undo, copy mode, the models used, offline operation, the privacy claims and uninstall were not tested. The built-in search and document chat (Knowledge OS) were not part of the session; the tester opened them afterwards and saw a chat answer with source markers, but did not check the answers (see the correction chapter).
verdict.fit: The tester sees it as a promising tool that needs small tests and repeated fine-tuning, and plans to retest next year when he has more business documents. He had seen the MCP link, possibly with a retrieval layer on top, as the interesting direction. The developer has since pointed out that search and document chat are already built in, so that layer exists (see the correction chapter). No decision on continued use is stated.

chapters.title: Earlier attempt, installer and first launch
items: This was the tester's second session. In the first he clicked through without reading the guidance, found the app not self-explanatory and thinks he made setup mistakes. What went wrong is not recorded.
He then wrote to the developer, who by his account reviewed the comments and addressed some issues within several days. No message is shown; the issues and the version are not recorded.
The installer window shows the app icon, labelled "StratoSort Stack", beside an Applications shortcut. Installer size is not recorded.

The app opens on a welcome screen: "Step 1 of 5, Start securely", a Guided and a Dashboard mode, and a main button "Organize files now, recommended for a first session", with side buttons for AI and model settings and smart folders. He chose guided steps because he wanted to follow the instructions this time. A notification bell shows a count; its content is not recorded.
Two cards offer other starting points: Guided steps and Dashboard.
The models offered, chosen and downloaded, their size and the setup time are not recorded. The directory lists about 7 GB for the base models.

chapters.title: Folders and the dry run
items: The tester asked the app to read a whole folder and it did not, so he gave it individual files. The folder, any message and the cause are not recorded; no screenshot.

He built the folder structure in Finder, an input folder plus output folders, and found that easier than doing it in the app. The app speaks of smart folders with a description, while he thinks in input and output folders. In-app folder creation does exist (see the banner in the review step).
The output folders were on an external SSD, as the move list and the MCP table show. The tester says the first attempt had not accepted it; the cause was not recorded.

A first test on five files showed where each would go; the screen says "Nothing has moved". Two files were assigned: a Clarity CSV to Clarity at 43 % confidence and a picture to Pictures at 65 %. Three went to Uncategorized, each with a closest folder named: Clarity, Leftovers and excel GSc. His own review-notes file was among the three.

He was not convinced and wanted a form at that step to confirm or reject each result, instead of going back to edit the folders and run again. The screen offers "Edit Smart Folders" and "Analyze the other 281 files"; per-file choices appear later, in the review step.

chapters.title: Analysis and review
items: The other 281 files were analysed. The progress card shows "Analyzing 5 of 281 files, 2 % complete", the file being processed and a Stop button. Total analysis time is not recorded.

In the review step each file has a card with a checkbox, an editable suggested name, a category dropdown (best match plus other suggestions), a "Needs review" note with the reason, a confidence bar and a Details link. Whether every file was reviewed before the move is not recorded.

Details shows project, purpose, date, document type, method, length, a summary, keywords, reasoning and the extracted text. The tester reads this as the way to fine-tune the sorting and says some data is extracted and kept in what he calls a database; the screens show the extracted fields only.

For an Excel file the extracted text is 300 characters and ends with an ellipsis after the column headers and a few rows. Whether the limit applies to other file types or to the classification step is not known (assumption: it may explain weak matches on spreadsheets).

Two Search Console Excel exports of 6 KB each, named after the site URL, got descriptive suggested names but went to the fallback, although the note names "excel GSc", the tester's folder for them, as closest. The cause was not isolated.

A banner reads "126 files are uncategorized" and "103 are from Promptquorum. Want a Smart Folder for them?", with Create folder, Different folder and Reanalyze buttons. The suggestion appears to follow the site name in the file names, not the content type (assumption).

The tester first felt the match was 70 to 80 percent and revised this to about 40 percent not matched after seeing the uncategorized count. Taken against the 286 files, 126 would be 44 %; that is a calculation and assumes both counts refer to the same files.

chapters.title: Moving files
items: "Organize 286 files, moving files to their destinations" lists planned operations with green ticks and paths on the external SSD; step navigation is paused until the move finishes or is cancelled. The tester's own test-notes documents were among the files. The end of the move is not recorded.

The move list replaced original names with lowercase names and a date, for example "Gesamtansicht.jpeg" became "gesamtansicht-2026-10-20.jpeg" and "StratoSort hands on review.docx" became "stratosort-review-2026-11-12.docx". The tester wrote that renaming was not tried; the list shows it was applied in this run. The result was not checked on disk, and the origin of the dates is not shown.

One WhatsApp image of 126 KB was added on its own and got a card with a suggested name, Pictures as best match and 64 % confidence. The tester says single files from anywhere on the computer can be added and sorted with the rest, and he values this.
A second capture reads "Organize 75 files"; its relation to the 286-file run is not recorded, and neither end is shown.

chapters.title: A link to another local AI app over MCP
items: The app has an MCP screen listing four tools: search_documents, chat_with_documents, get_document_summary and list_smart_folders, with buttons that copy the setup for Claude Desktop, Cursor and Zed.

Because MCP is a standard protocol, the app can be linked to a standard LLM client: the setup buttons on that screen are for Claude Desktop, Cursor and Zed, and the tester linked it to Loci. The tester did not try Claude Desktop, Cursor or Zed, so no connection to those was verified.
A line on that screen says: "These tools only read. None of them moves, renames or deletes files."
The tester says he had to "backwards engineer" the connection to another local AI app. What failed and what he changed are not recorded.

The client, Loci, reports "Strato is connected and offers 4 tools" at a local address and says for each tool that it does not say whether it can change things. That the tools carry no read-only marker is an assumption; the app says they only read.
Loci's server list shows PromptQuorum with 27 tools and Strato with 4 tools, both connected.

list_smart_folders returned a table with folder, file count, description and destination path. Visible rows: Uncategorized 53, Pictures 8, excel GSc 196. The 53 does not match the 126 seen earlier in the review step; the time between the two is not recorded, so they are not reconciled.
Before the search, Loci asked "Allow Strato to run search_documents?" with the query "Clarity data", a local address, and the buttons Allow once and Decline.

search_documents with the query "Clarity data" returned four CSV files from the Clarity folder, each with a one-line description. The client's reply guesses that the source is Microsoft Clarity or a similar tool. Correctness against the file contents was not checked; the reply continues below the visible area.

He says it does not yet look like a retrieval system but moves toward a dataset that outside tools can query. He called only two of the four tools; get_document_summary and chat_with_documents were not called. Correction: StratoSort does have a retrieval system of its own (see the correction chapter below).

chapters.title: Correction: StratoSort has built-in search and chat (Knowledge OS)
items: After this test was first published, the developer, Ben Kennedy, wrote that StratoSort already includes a retrieval system (RAG) with its own search and document chat, and that he should have pointed the tester to it more clearly. This page said the opposite in several places; those statements are corrected here and marked in the text. Thank you, Ben, for pointing it out.

Per the developer: pressing Cmd+K on the Mac, or clicking Knowledge OS in the navigation, opens five views. Search finds analysed files by meaning or keywords, combining vector similarity with keyword search. Chat answers questions about those files with source-document citations. Relate is a graph of related files and clusters. Atlas is a map of the library with similar files grouped together. Timeline lists analysed files by date.

The tester opened Knowledge OS afterwards. The Search view has a box reading "Describe what you're looking for..." and three search tips: natural language such as "vacation photos from beach", file types such as "PDF documents", and content descriptions such as "spreadsheet with budget". No search was run in the screenshot.

The Timeline view lists analysed files, each with a folder label that is cut off in the narrow window (for example CLARI…, SEO D… and STRAT…) and the file name. The visible entries are the test's own exports and notes.

The top bar of the Relate view reads 5 smart folders and 550 files indexed; the 550 differs from the 286 files of the sorting run, and the reason is not recorded. The graph shows 14 clusters, 47 bridges, 0 scattered files, a health grade of A (92) with 1 finding, and 14 nodes with 28 links. A suggestion card names two files as 83% related although they sit in different folders.

In Chat, a conversation named "bing data" holds an assistant answer about Bing sessions with two numbered source markers beside the text, and a persona selector reading "Professional Re…" (cut off). Whether the numbers in the answer match the source files was not checked.
A second capture of the same chat shows the status "Analyzing documents..." while the answer text is already on screen without the source markers, and the sidebar reads "No conversations yet".

The developer describes the mechanism: StratoSort indexes extracted file content locally, retrieves the relevant material for a question and supplies it to the model, which answers from the user's documents. No other app or MCP is needed for this. MCP gives another app access to the library, while the built-in Search and Chat run inside StratoSort.

The developer says the default setup runs locally, including embeddings, retrieval and chat. Optional cloud providers can be enabled but are not required. With MCP, whether retrieved content stays local also depends on the client and model that are connected. The tester has not verified this.

On the tester's point that sorting needs clear folder descriptions and feedback, the developer says this is separate from training or fine-tuning the language model. On the Organize screen, a file's destination can be changed before the move. After two different files with the same type and label are moved from the suggested folder into the same other folder, StratoSort learns that routing correction; it can be reviewed in Settings > Performance > Memory & Rules. The tester has not tried this.

The developer says recent releases addressed the issues from the tester's first test: conflicting filenames, clearer previews and full destination lists, external-drive access, more consistent spreadsheet routing, and clearer reporting when files do not move. Version 5.4.0 added a five-file trial before large batches, safer handling of overlapping folders and "Needs review" for weak matches instead of a forced destination, and fixed growing memory use during long batches and reduced repeated analysis. The tester has not retested these versions.

What this changes: the statement that a retrieval layer would have to be added was wrong, and the remark that the app does not yet look like a retrieval system does not hold. What stays: the screens were seen once, no answer was checked against the files, and the sorting results of the original session are unchanged.

chapters.title: Decision
items: The notes end with an overall view and no decision on continued use.

In his understanding the app sorts files, needs time to fine-tune, and works best with a small start and repeated checking, adjusting the smart folders as you go. He used moving, not copying, and did not try the rewording and renaming functions.

He plans to set up a legal entity next year and to repeat the test with more documents to see whether it can keep his folder system in order. His interest is that combination with MCP and perhaps a retrieval layer on top. Correction: that layer is already built in (see the correction chapter above).
"You need to start small with some files and then check it, check it, check it, and fine-tune all the rules."
"Having worked in consulting, I know the worst thing is always keeping an order in file systems, and then afterwards finding something."

severity_note: Severity is the impact on a first-time user. Proposed, not measured. Info marks a finding that is neither a problem nor a strength; Positive marks something that worked well.

fits: Mac users with mixed, private document folders who accept starting small, checking often and tuning the folder descriptions (assumption from one session).
not_fits: Anyone who expects accurate sorting after the first pass.
Anyone who needs commercial use without checking the licence: the directory lists a noncommercial licence and a paid per-seat licence for commercial use.
audience.retest: Retest on a new major version, after the issues the developer addressed are shipped, or when the tester has the company documents next year. Cover: record the app version and the models; run a known test set and count matched against uncategorized; the spreadsheet text limit; undo; copy mode; the built-in Search and Chat (check answers and source markers against the files, and try Atlas); get_document_summary and chat_with_documents over MCP; the changes the developer lists for version 5.4.0; offline use with traffic inspected; runtime memory; uninstall; the licence terms.
